0.0.n: Signals readiness to move on to the results.

0.2.n: Part of ということで, a set phrase used to transition to the next topic.

0.3.n: こと refers broadly to the preceding situation within the transition phrase ということで.

0.4.n: で completes ということで, connecting the preceding situation to what comes next.

0.6.n: A stretched hesitation sound that gives the speaker time to think.

0.8.n: Refers to the points earned by the participants.

0.9.n: Marks 得点 as what was tallied.

0.10.n: Past form of 集計する, indicating the counting is complete.

0.11.n: Short for の; presents the completed tally as background for the announcement.

0.12.n: Makes the explanation in んです polite.

0.13.n: Literally suggests contrast, but here softly leads into the next statement rather than opposing it.

1.0.n: A brief polite acknowledgment of the preceding statement.

2.0.n: 発表する becomes 発表して, then adds いく for proceeding and たい for wanting to do it.

2.1.n: Marks the preceding wish as what the speaker thinks.

2.2.n: Polite form of 思う; with たいと, it gently expresses the speaker's intention.

3.0.n: A family name, placed before the given name 柔太朗.

3.1.n: This character belongs to the given name 柔太朗; it is not a separate word here.

3.2.n: These characters complete the given name 柔太朗.

3.3.n: 君 follows the full name as a familiar, respectful suffix often used for boys or young men.

3.5.n: A number plus ポイント states the contestant's score.

4.0.n: Repeats the score just announced, without needing a verb.

5.0.n: A family name, placed before the given name 舜太.

5.1.n: This character begins the given name 舜太; it is not a separate word here.

5.2.n: This character completes the given name 舜太.

5.3.n: 君 adds a familiar, respectful tone when addressing or referring to this young man.

5.5.n: A number plus ポイント gives Sono's score.

6.0.n: This character belongs to the family name 塩﨑, not the ordinary word for salt here.

6.2.n: This character begins the given name 太智; read the name as a whole.

6.3.n: This character completes the given name 太智.

6.4.n: 君 follows the contestant's name with a familiar, respectful tone.

7.0.n: Completes the score announcement begun with Shiozaki's name in the previous line.

8.0.n: Normally means winning a championship; here it introduces the person who took first place.

8.1.n: Marks 優勝 as the topic before identifying who won.

8.2.n: This character is part of the family name 塩﨑.

8.4.n: This character begins the given name 太智.

8.5.n: This character completes the given name 太智.

8.6.n: 君 adds familiar respect after the winner's full name.

8.7.n: Politely completes the statement identifying the winner.

9.0.n: Casual shortened form of やっぱり, showing the result matches expectations.

9.1.n: Expresses admiration for someone living up to their reputation or ability.

9.2.n: Makes the admiring comment polite; it does not mark past tense.

9.3.n: Invites the listener to share the speaker's admiration.

10.0.n: An English loanword referring here to expressive responses, such as gestures or exclamations.

10.1.n: Placed before でかい to indicate the greatest degree among those compared.

10.2.n: でかい is a casual alternative to 大きい; adding です makes the ending polite.

10.3.n: Seeks agreement with the observation about his reactions.

10.5.n: Casual やっぱり, reinforcing that the observation fits what the speaker expected.

10.6.n: Adds a friendly appeal for agreement to the trailing afterthought.

11.0.n: 僕 plus ら refers to the speaker and their group; 僕 is commonly used by male speakers.

11.1.n: て-form of 含める; combines with も to mean even if included.

11.2.n: After 含めて, emphasizes that adding the speaker's group does not change who ranks first.

11.3.n: Modifies でかい to rank his reactions above everyone else's.

11.4.n: Casual adjective describing the size or intensity of his reactions, not his body.

11.5.n: Casual contraction of ので, giving a reason while leaving the conclusion unstated.

0.lit: All right. So, um, the scores we tallied, but…
0.tip: んですけども gives background and softly sets up the next statement; it need not introduce a disagreement.

1.tip: はい can simply acknowledge another speaker rather than answer a question.

2.lit: I think we want to proceed with announcing.
2.tip: たいと思います is a polite, softened way to announce what you intend to do.

3.tip: Japanese names normally put the family name first, and 君 is a suffix rather than part of the name.

4.tip: A score can stand alone as a complete spoken response without a verb.

5.tip: 舜 and 太 belong to one given name, 舜太, rather than functioning as separate words.

6.tip: The speaker pauses after the contestant's name, leaving the score for the next line.

7.tip: ポイント stays the same whether the score is one point or many points.

8.lit: As for the championship, it is Shiozaki Daichi!
8.tip: 優勝は followed by a person's name is a natural way to announce the winner.

9.tip: さすが praises someone for living up to expectations; the Japanese does not explicitly use past tense here.

10.lit: Reactions are biggest, aren't they, after all, you know.
10.tip: でかい is a casual word for big and can describe exaggerated reactions.

11.lit: Even including us, his are biggest, because…
11.tip: て-form plus も means even if; 含めても expands the comparison to include the speakers.
